chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Abd al-Rahman from Abd Allah ibn Sinan said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who departed from Jumu'ah until he reached Mina, and a hindrance occurred to him so he did not throw [the pebbles] until the sun set. He said: 'He should throw when he rises in the morning twice: once for what was missed by him, and the second for the day on which he rises in it. And he should distinguish between the two, so that one of them is in the early morning, and it is for yesterday, and the other is at the time of the sun's decline.'

key_terms.جَمْعٍ: Jumu'ah, the second station of Hajj where pilgrims stay overnight
key_terms.زَوَالِ الشَّمْسِ: Sun's decline (midday), a specific time for ritual actions
key_terms.عَارِضٌ: A hindrance or obstacle preventing the ritual
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, the site of the pebble-throwing ritual

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for making up missed pebble-throwing in Mina if one was hindered?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the fiqh of *qada* (making up) missed *rami* pillars when a pilgrim is delayed in Mina, emphasizing the distinction between compensating for the previous day's obligation and fulfilling the current day's requirement. The specific timing—early morning for the makeup and after solar noon (*zawal*) for the current day—reflects the Shia juristic preference for separating distinct ritual acts to ensure clarity and validity. This ruling underscores the flexibility within the Hajj rituals to accommodate unforeseen hindrances (*'arid*) without invalidating the pilgrimage.
